slides.title: Things your doctor wishes you'd just ask

slides.q: Why did my poop turn red after eating beets?
slides.a: Beets contain a deep red pigment that some people don't fully break down, so poop or pee can turn pink or red for a day or two. It's harmless, and when it shows up in pee it's called beeturia. Worth seeing a doctor if you see red without eating beets, or stool looks black or tarry.

slides.q: Why do I get a headache after sitting at my desk all day?
slides.a: Hours hunched over a screen can tighten the muscles in your neck, shoulders, and scalp, causing tension headaches. Eye strain, not drinking enough water, and stress add to it. Short breaks, a screen at eye level, and stretching can help. Worth seeing a doctor if headaches are severe, sudden, or happening most days.

slides.q: Why do my ears suddenly feel hot?
slides.a: Your ears have lots of tiny blood vessels close to the skin, so they flush easily when you're embarrassed, angry, warm, or have had a drink. That rush of blood makes them feel hot and look red. It's usually harmless and fades quickly. Worth seeing a doctor if it comes with pain, swelling, or keeps coming back.

slides.q: Is it bad to hold in a fart?
slides.a: Holding one in now and then won't hurt you, but the gas doesn't disappear. Some gets reabsorbed, and the rest usually comes out later anyway. Holding it in a lot can cause bloating and cramps, so letting it out when you can is the comfiest option. Worth seeing a doctor if gas comes with ongoing pain.

slides.q: Why do my nipples get hard when I'm cold?
slides.a: Nipples have tiny muscles that contract with cold, touch, or even a sudden rush of emotion, the same kind of reflex behind goosebumps. It happens to everyone, any gender, and it's completely normal. Worth seeing a doctor if you notice discharge, a new lump, skin changes, or a nipple that starts turning inward.
